name: GCOPTER (MINCO) — geometrically-constrained MINCO trajectory optimizer (ZJU-FAST-Lab)
license: MIT (verified via GitHub API: spdx_id MIT, default branch `main`). Vendor-friendly — can be copied straight into sando-core and linked into the certified core with attribution.
trajectory_format: Header-only, Eigen-only. Committed trajectory is `Trajectory<5>` defined in gcopter/include/gcopter/trajectory.hpp. It is `std::vector<Piece<5>>` with: `int getPieceNum()`, `const Piece<5>& operator[](int i)` (this is the verified accessor; some forks alias it `getPiece(i)`). Each `Piece<5>` exposes `double getDuration()` and `const CoefficientMat& getCoeffMat()` where `typedef Eigen::Matrix<double,3,D+1> CoefficientMat` => a 3x6 MONOMIAL (power-basis) matrix in REAL time tau in [0,dur]. Verified power order (getPos loop `for(i=D;i>=0;i--){pos+=tn*coeffMat.col(i); tn*=t;}` with tn starting at 1, no /duration): col(0)=coeff of tau^5 (HIGHEST power), col(5)=coeff of tau^0 (constant). Rows = x,y,z. The trajectory is PRODUCED by the MINCO layer `minco::MINCO_S3NU` (minco.hpp, includes only gcopter/trajectory.hpp + <Eigen/Eigen>, NO ROS): `setConditions(const Eigen::Matrix3d& headPVA, const Eigen::Matrix3d& tailPVA, const int& pieceNum)`, `setParameters(const Eigen::Matrix3Xd& inPs, const Eigen::VectorXd& ts)`, `getTrajectory(Trajectory<5>& traj)`. Full collision-aware pipeline = `gcopter::GCOPTER_PolytopeSFC` (gcopter.hpp): `setup(timeWeight, initPVA, termPVA, std::vector<Eigen::MatrixX4d> hPolys, lenPerPiece, smoothFactor, intResolution, magnitudeBounds, penaltyWeights, physicalParams)` then `double optimize(Trajectory<5>& traj, relCostTol)` — same Trajectory<5> output type.
adapter_to_bseg: Same deg-5 power->Bernstein path we already use for MINCO, with TWO fixes (reverse columns, scale by dur^j). Per piece i of the Trajectory<5>: (1) dur = piece.getDuration(); t0 = sum of getDuration() over pieces 0..i-1 (pieces are sequential from traj t=0, matching locatePieceIdx). (2) Read C = piece.getCoeffMat() (3x6, real-time tau in [0,dur], DESCENDING power: col(0)=tau^5..col(5)=const). (3) Reparametrize tau=s*dur, s in [0,1]: ascending normalized coeff for power j is a_j = C.col(5-j) * dur^j  (j=0..5; the col(5-j) reverses descending->ascending, dur^j absorbs the real-time->[0,1] rescale). (4) Apply OUR existing degree-5 power->Bernstein matrix C2B_matrix() from cpp/include/sando_cpp/minjerk_traj.hpp (the 6x6 lower-triangular /60 matrix == monomial->Bernstein for deg 5): Bernstein control point b_k = sum_{j=0..k} C2B[k][j] * a_j, equivalently b_k = sum_j [C(k,j)/C(5,j)] a_j, done per coordinate x,y,z. (5) Emit BSeg{ bern = {b_0..b_5} as Eigen::Vector3d, t0, dur }; degree 5 >= 2 OK. (6) std::vector<BSeg> -> certify_segments_vs_sphere / _above_plane exactly as minco_to_segments output. This is literally minco_to_segments with col reversal + dur^j; reuse C2B_matrix().
runnable: output-only-cert for the full GCOPTER_PolytopeSFC SFC pipeline (needs a polytope safe-flight-corridor + init path as input); fully-runnable for the minco::MINCO_S3NU smoother layer (waypoints+durations -> Trajectory<5>). Recommended graft = build the MINCO layer capi (fully-runnable) and/or certify a Trajectory<5> emitted by the full optimizer (output-only).
advantage: This IS the canonical MINCO reference implementation our whole certificate is named after (continuous-time conformal-Bernstein deficit on MINCO). Certifying GCOPTER's OWN committed Trajectory<5> — not our re-implemented quintic — is the strongest possible planner-agnostic demonstration: same degree-5, byte-identical C2B path, but a third-party SOTA optimizer doing joint spatial-temporal optimization inside safe flight corridors. It is the academic gold-standard multicopter optimizer, so 'our cert gates GCOPTER' is a headline baseline. Also lets us A/B EGO (B-spline) vs GCOPTER (MINCO) under the identical certificate.
build_or_bridge: Header-only + Eigen only, no ROS in the core. RECOMMENDED (fully-runnable smoother): vendor trajectory.hpp + minco.hpp, write gcopter_capi.so mirroring ego_capi.so — `gcopter_create()`, `gcopter_set_minco(head3x3 PVA, tail3x3 PVA, inner_points 3x(N-1), durations N)` -> MINCO_S3NU.setConditions/setParameters/getTrajectory, then `gcopter_piece_count()` and `gcopter_piece(i, out: t0,dur, 3x6 coeff)`. Python side does the reverse+dur^j+C2B -> BSeg (or do C2B in C++ and return Bernstein control points directly, like ego_capi already does). OPTIONAL (full collision pipeline, output-only-cert): additionally vendor gcopter.hpp, sfc_gen.hpp, firi.hpp, geo_utils.hpp, quickhull.hpp, sdlp.hpp, lbfgs.hpp, flatness.hpp, voxel_map.hpp, voxel_dilater.hpp, root_finder.hpp; feed a point cloud -> voxel_map -> sfc_gen corridors -> setup()+optimize() -> Trajectory<5> -> same adapter. Build flags as in CLAUDE.md: g++ -O2 -shared -fPIC -std=c++17 -w -o capi/gcopter_capi.so capi/gcopter_capi.cpp -Iinclude -I../cpp/include -I../cpp/third_party/eigen.
vendor_files: MINIMAL (recommended): gcopter/include/gcopter/trajectory.hpp + gcopter/include/gcopter/minco.hpp + Eigen (reuse cpp/third_party/eigen). DROP everything else and the whole ROS layer (gcopter/src/global_planner.cpp node, misc/visualizer.hpp, launch/, config/, CMake catkin bits). FULL pipeline adds: gcopter.hpp, sfc_gen.hpp, firi.hpp, geo_utils.hpp, quickhull.hpp, sdlp.hpp, lbfgs.hpp, flatness.hpp, voxel_map.hpp, voxel_dilater.hpp, root_finder.hpp (all under gcopter/include/gcopter/, all header-only, Eigen-only).
gotchas: (1) Power order is DESCENDING (col(0)=tau^5) — opposite of our ascending C2B; must reverse columns (col(5-j)) or you silently certify a mirrored polynomial. (2) getCoeffMat() is REAL-time, so the dur^j rescale is mandatory before C2B (skip it and the Bernstein hull is wrong by dur powers). (3) Trajectory<5> is for s=3 (min-jerk); a min-snap setup would be Trajectory<7> — adapter must read D=traj degree, not hard-code 5 (cert already handles any degree>=2, just size bern to D+1 and use a deg-D power->Bernstein matrix instead of the deg-5 C2B). (4) Full GCOPTER_PolytopeSFC needs polytope corridors + an init path + physicalParams/flatness — that is the heavy part; if we only want the certified trajectory, prefer feeding it corridors offline and certifying the emitted Trajectory<5> (output-only). (5) MINCO_S3NU.setConditions head/tail are 3x3 PVA (cols = pos,vel,acc), not just position.

name: am_traj (AM-Traj) — alternating-minimization min-jerk with simultaneous spatial-temporal optimal time allocation (ZJU-FAST-Lab)
license: GPL-3.0 (verified via GitHub API: spdx_id GPL-3.0, default branch `master`). COPYLEFT — this is the biggest practical gotcha (see gotchas): do NOT statically link into the certified core; keep it as an isolated comparison binary / separate process or use it output-only.
trajectory_format: Header-only (include/am_traj/am_traj.hpp + include/am_traj/root_finder.hpp), Eigen + STL only, NO ROS in core (ROS only in example/). Optimizer class `AmTraj`; constructor `AmTraj(double wT, double wA, double wJ, double mVr, double mAr, int mIts, double eps)` (time/accel/jerk weights, max vel, max acc, max iters, rel tol). Trajectory generators (each returns a `Trajectory` by value): `Trajectory genOptimalTrajDT(const std::vector<Eigen::Vector3d>& wayPs, Eigen::Vector3d iniVel, Eigen::Vector3d iniAcc, Eigen::Vector3d finVel, Eigen::Vector3d finAcc)` (optimize durations), plus genOptimalTrajDC and genOptimalTrajDTC (joint durations+coeffs). `Trajectory` = vector of quintic `Piece` (constexpr TrajOrder=5, TrajDim=3): `int getPieceNum()`, `const Piece& operator[](int i)`, Piece `double getDuration()`, `CoefficientMat getCoeffMat(bool normalized=false)` with `typedef Eigen::Matrix<double,3,6> CoefficientMat`. STORED member is `nCoeffMat` = NORMALIZED coeffs on s in [0,1] laid out [c5*T^5, c4*T^4, .., c1*T, c0] (descending power); getPos does `t/=duration` then Horner on nCoeffMat. getCoeffMat(false) divides the T-powers back out -> real-time coeffs; getCoeffMat(true) returns the normalized [0,1] coeffs directly. Either way col(0)=highest power, col(5)=constant.
adapter_to_bseg: Even simpler than GCOPTER because am_traj already stores the s in [0,1] normalized coeffs. Per piece i: dur = piece.getDuration(); t0 = sum of getDuration() over pieces 0..i-1. Take N = piece.getCoeffMat(true) (3x6, s in [0,1], DESCENDING power: col(0)=s^5..col(5)=const) — this is exactly the normalized scaled coeff vector, no dur^j scaling needed. Form ascending coeffs a_j = N.col(5-j) (j=0..5, reverse columns). Apply OUR deg-5 C2B_matrix() (monomial->Bernstein): b_k = sum_{j<=k} C2B[k][j]*a_j per coordinate -> 6 Bernstein control points. Emit BSeg{bern={b_0..b_5}, t0, dur}; degree 5>=2 OK; std::vector<BSeg> -> certify_segments_vs_sphere/_above_plane. (Equivalent path with getCoeffMat(false): a_j = C.col(5-j)*dur^j, then same C2B — identical result, mirrors the GCOPTER adapter exactly.)
runnable: fully-runnable (header-only, builds in seconds, no corridors/map/solver needed — it is a pure waypoint smoother). License caveat aside, technically trivial to run end-to-end.
advantage: Pure analytic minimum-jerk with closed-form gradient AND simultaneous spatial-temporal (time-allocation) optimality — the direct precursor to MINCO and an extremely fast smoother. Unlike EGO and GCOPTER it has NO collision/SFC module, so it isolates the cleanest baseline: 'smooth quintic poly (it provides speed) + OUR cert (we provide the only safety)'. Same degree-5 as our MINCO -> identical C2B path, so it is the lowest-friction third-party planner to graft and a strong fast A/B point against EGO. Great for showing the cert gates an UNSAFE-by-construction smoother (it will sometimes cut corners into obstacles -> cert correctly refuses -> maneuver tournament reroutes).
build_or_bridge: Vendor the two headers, write amtraj_capi.so (mirror ego_capi.so): `amtraj_create(wT,wA,wJ,vmax,amax,iters,eps)`, `amtraj_gen(double* waypoints 3xK, ini_vel, ini_acc, fin_vel, fin_acc, int which=DT/DC/DTC)` -> store the returned Trajectory, `amtraj_piece_count()`, `amtraj_piece(i, out t0,dur, 3x6 coeff)` (or do reverse+C2B in C++ and return the 6 Bernstein control points directly like ego_capi). Python feeds the SAME waypoint path EGO/GCOPTER use (e.g. EGO's control-point path or the front-end path) for a fair A/B. Build: g++ -O2 -shared -fPIC -std=c++17 -w -o capi/amtraj_capi.so capi/amtraj_capi.cpp -Iinclude -I../cpp/third_party/eigen. To respect GPL, build this .so as a standalone optional plugin loaded by a separate harness, not linked into the MIT/closed cert core.
vendor_files: include/am_traj/am_traj.hpp + include/am_traj/root_finder.hpp (that's all — header-only, Eigen-only). DROP: example/ (the ROS demo node + launch + rviz), CMakeLists catkin bits, images/.
gotchas: (1) GPL-3.0 COPYLEFT is the dominant gotcha — linking am_traj into the certified core would force-GPL it; keep it as an isolated comparison binary or use output-only (capture its emitted Trajectory). (2) am_traj takes WAYPOINTS, not a corridor and not obstacles — it does zero collision avoidance, so to be a fair baseline feed it the identical waypoint path the other planners use; expect it to occasionally cut into obstacles (that is the point — the cert is the gate). (3) Descending power order (col(0)=s^5) — reverse columns vs our ascending C2B. (4) nCoeffMat vs coeffMat: use getCoeffMat(true) to skip the dur^j scaling (it is already normalized to s in [0,1]); if you use getCoeffMat(false) you must multiply by dur^j. (5) genOptimalTrajDT vs DTC change the time allocation but the output Trajectory/Piece layout is identical, so the adapter is unchanged.

name: TGK-Planner (Topology Guided Kinodynamic, KRRT* + closed-form BVP)
trajectory_format: Committed trajectory is a `Trajectory` = std::vector<Piece> (planning/poly_traj_utils/include/poly_traj_utils/traj_utils.hpp). Getters: front-end `KRRTPlanner::getTraj(Trajectory& traj)` (kino_plan/krrtplanner.h:49) and back-end `TrajOptimizer::getTraj(Trajectory& traj)` (poly_opt/traj_optimizer.h:24) — use the OPTIMIZED one as the committed traj. Per piece: `Piece::getCoeffMat(false)` -> Eigen::Matrix<double,3,6> (CoefficientMat = TrajDim x TrajOrder+1) of REAL monomial coefficients, row=dim(x,y,z), column k = coeff of t^(5-k) (DESCENDING power: col0=c5 of t^5 ... col5=c0). `Piece::getDuration()` -> double. Fixed at compile time: TrajOrder=5 (quintic), TrajDim=3. p(t)=sum_j c_j t^j over local t in [0,duration].
adapter_to_bseg: Basis change = monomial(power) -> Bernstein, degree 5, via OUR EXISTING fixed deg-5 C2B matrix (C2B_matrix() in minjerk_traj.hpp == C2B_int()/60 in bernstein_cert.hpp). This is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the shipped MINCO path, so reuse minco_to_segments verbatim. EXACT steps: (1) Build a sando::MinjerkTraj m: m.M = traj.getPieceNum(); for piece i: m.T(i)=traj[i].getDuration(); cm=traj[i].getCoeffMat(false); fill ASCENDING power with column reversal: m.c(6*i + j, d) = cm(d, 5 - j) for j=0..5,d=0..2; set cumulative timing m.cum(0)=0, m.cum(i+1)=m.cum(i)+m.T(i), m.t_end=m.cum(M). (2) auto segs = sando::bcert::minco_to_segments(m) -- this folds a_j=c_j*Ti^j then P_k=C2B*a to physical deg-5 Bernstein control points and sets BSeg.t0=cum(i), BSeg.dur=T(i). (3) sando::bcert::certify_segments_vs_sphere(segs, c0,vel,acc, R, t_hi, 16, v_eff, delta). Equivalent direct form (no MinjerkTraj): a_j = cm(d,5-j)*Ti^j; P_k = sum_j (C2B_int[k][j]/60)*a_j. Segment timing: TGK pieces are already per-segment polynomials (NOT a global B-spline, so NO knot insertion needed, unlike EGO); local time is [0,duration]; BSeg.t0 = cumulative prefix sum of prior durations, BSeg.dur = piece duration -- exactly the MINCO timing map.
build_or_bridge: Build a standalone libtgk_capi.so mirroring ego/capi/ego_capi.so. NO external solver needed (the min-effort optimize is closed-form, feasibility uses TGK's self-contained header root_finder.hpp -- no Gurobi/Mosek/NLopt/Ceres), so it compiles with the same `g++ -O2 -shared -fPIC -std=c++17` recipe as EGO. Steps: shim ros::NodeHandle (params -> hard-coded defaults like ego_create), stub occ_grid/pos_checker.h `PosChecker` against our point-cloud occupancy grid (reuse the EGO grid_map cloud-feed pattern in ego_capi.cpp: update_point_cloud + getInflateOccupancy), stub visualization_utils `VisualRviz` to no-ops. capi entrypoints: tgk_create / tgk_set_map / tgk_update_cloud(pts,cam) / tgk_replan(start PVA, goal PV) -> calls KRRTPlanner.plan then TrajOptimizer, then KRRTPlanner/TrajOptimizer::getTraj(Trajectory&) -> build_segs() (the adapter above) -> then literally copy ego_capi's tgk_certify / tgk_certify_horizontal / tgk_certify_above bodies (same certify_segments_* calls). Drive from a tgk_bridge.py cloned from ego_bridge.py.
vendor_files: COPY: planning/poly_traj_utils/{include/poly_traj_utils/traj_utils.hpp, include/poly_traj_utils/root_finder.hpp, src/poly_traj_utils.cpp}; planning/poly_opt/{include/poly_opt/traj_optimizer.h, src/traj_optimizer.cpp}; planning/kino_plan/{include/kino_plan/[krrtplanner.h, bvp_solver.h, bias_sampler.h, kdtree.h, node_utils.h, raycast.h], src/[krrtplanner.cpp, bvp_solver.cpp, bias_sampler.cpp, raycast.cpp]}. WRITE a stub occ_grid/pos_checker.h (PosChecker) backed by a point-cloud occupancy grid. DROP: decision/state_machine, uav_simulator, self_msgs_and_srvs (ROS msgs), visualization_utils (replace VisualRviz with a no-op stub header), every ros::NodeHandle/rosparam call (replace with the ego_capi-style shim), rviz.
advantage: The ONLY sampling-based kinodynamic baseline (Kinodynamic RRT* front-end + closed-form fixed-final-state BVP back-end) -- a fundamentally different trajectory-generation paradigm from EGO's gradient-pushed B-spline and our optimization MINCO. Yet it emits a NATIVE quintic polynomial in the exact same power basis as MINCO, so it certifies through our deg-5 path with ZERO new basis math (reuses minco_to_segments verbatim). Strongest single piece of planner-agnostic evidence: a totally different planner class, certified by the identical core. Bonus: no commercial solver, so it builds as trivially as EGO.
license: GPL-3.0 (copyleft). Fine for internal eval; keep our cert header/capi as a thin separable layer if distribution is ever considered.
gotchas: (1) getCoeffMat columns are DESCENDING power (col0=t^5 coeff) -- MUST reverse (5-j) when filling MinjerkTraj.c (ascending), else the polynomial is mirrored. (2) getTraj overwrites the internal traj_ on every replan -- snapshot each verdict before the next replan (same hazard as EGO local_data_). (3) Pieces are independent BVP solutions; junction continuity is whatever the optimizer enforced, but the per-segment cert does not care (each BSeg certified on its own [0,dur]). (4) TrajOrder=5/TrajDim=3 are compile-time constexpr -- the front-end KRRT* needs a working PosChecker fed the SAME point cloud we give EGO, or it returns no path. (5) RRT* front-end is the slow part (~0.05-0.10 s), optimize is ~0.5-2 ms -- budget the replan timeout accordingly.

name: Btraj (flight-corridor piecewise Bezier, Gao et al. ICRA 2018)
trajectory_format: Native piecewise Bezier. Generated by `int TrajectoryGenerator::BezierPloyCoeffGeneration(const vector<Cube>& corridor, const MatrixXd& MQM, const MatrixXd& pos, const MatrixXd& vel, const MatrixXd& acc, double maxVel, double maxAcc, int traj_order, double minimize_order, double margin, bool isLimitVel, bool isLimitAcc, double& obj, MatrixXd& PolyCoeff)` (include/trajectory_generator.h). It fills `PolyCoeff` (in the node held as `MatrixXd _bezier_coeff`): rows = _seg_num (= corridor.size()), cols = 3*(traj_order+1). Per-row column layout = [x_0..x_n | y_0..y_n | z_0..z_n] with ctrl_num1D = traj_order+1. Per-segment durations: `VectorXd _seg_time`, _seg_time(i)=corridor[i].t. Degree: `int _traj_order` (rosparam optimization/poly_order, DEFAULT 10). CRITICAL: control points are stored NORMALIZED by segment time -- physical eval is pos = _seg_time(i) * sum_k C(n,k)*coeff(i, d*ctrl_num1D+k)*s^k*(1-s)^(n-k), s=t_local/_seg_time(i) (b_traj_node.cpp getPosFromBezier + lines 333-336). _C(j)=C(traj_order,j) binomial from bezier_base getC().
adapter_to_bseg: Basis change = IDENTITY (already Bernstein/Bezier of degree n=traj_order; our BSeg.bern ARE Bezier control points). Only a per-segment seg_time un-scaling + a column-block reshape. EXACT steps: n = traj_order; ctrl = n+1; t0 = 0; for i in 0.._seg_num-1: BSeg s; s.dur = _seg_time(i); s.t0 = t0; s.bern.resize(n+1); for k=0..n: s.bern[k] = _seg_time(i) * Eigen::Vector3d( PolyCoeff(i, k), PolyCoeff(i, ctrl + k), PolyCoeff(i, 2*ctrl + k) );  segs.push_back(s); t0 += _seg_time(i). Then certify_segments_vs_sphere(segs, ...). The seg_time(i) MULTIPLY is mandatory -- it recovers the physical-space control points (Btraj's getPosFromBezier returns the unscaled hull then multiplies by seg_time). Index k ascending 0..n maps 1:1 to bern[0..n] (Btraj's _C(k)*s^k*(1-s)^(n-k) is exactly our Bernstein convention, no reorder). Segment timing: corridor[i].t = _seg_time(i) in physical seconds; BSeg.t0 = prefix sum of prior _seg_time. With default n=10 the deficit is degree 2n=20 -> use the GENERIC certify_segments_vs_sphere (any-degree, n>=2), NOT the hard-coded quintic certify_traj_vs_sphere.
build_or_bridge: Output-only: do NOT build the full planner (back-end needs commercial Mosek). Instead get ONE trajectory in its representation and feed the emitted control points. Two ways to obtain it: (a) run the original Btraj ROS node once and add ~6 lines right after BezierPloyCoeffGeneration in src/b_traj_node.cpp to dump _bezier_coeff, _seg_time, _traj_order to .npz/.csv; or (b) use the Mosek-free fork JialunLi/Btraj_osqp (OSQP) to regenerate trajectories without a Mosek license. Then in Python load the dump, apply the IDENTITY adapter above to build the BSeg list, and certify via a thin capi that accepts a flat BSeg array (a 10-line `certify_bseg_array()` extern-C wrapping certify_segments_vs_sphere). FULLY-RUNNABLE variant if desired: vendor the generator + corridor front-end and swap Mosek->OSQP (see vendor_files), ~24-30h.
vendor_files: Output-only path: NONE to build -- only add a dump print to src/b_traj_node.cpp (or trajectory_generator.cpp) after the QP solve. FULLY-RUNNABLE variant: COPY include/{bezier_base.h, data_type.h, trajectory_generator.h}, src/{bezier_base.cpp, trajectory_generator.cpp}, and the corridor-generation portion of src/b_traj_node.cpp (JPS/A* + fast-marching + cube inflation). DROP: third_party/mosek (replace QP with OSQP, as Btraj_osqp does), the ROS node wiring, the PCL/ESDF map front-end (feed corridor + start/goal PVA directly), quadrotor_msgs, rviz/backward.hpp.
advantage: The canonical flight-corridor convex-program Bezier planner: its output is LITERALLY Bernstein control points carrying the convex-hull safety property, so the basis change into our BSeg is the IDENTITY -- the purest possible demonstration that our certificate is planner-agnostic (no monomial->Bernstein, no B-spline knot insertion, no MINVO; just a seg_time scale + reshape). Default degree-10 Bezier stresses the GENERIC any-degree path (deficit degree 2n=20) that cubic EGO and quintic MINCO never exercise -- proves the core scales past low degree. And the hard-corridor constraint paradigm is maximally different from EGO's gradient pushout / our soft penalty, giving real planner-class diversity at ~6h cost.
license: NO license file in the repo (all-rights-reserved by default). Output-only-cert consumes only emitted NUMBERS (control points), not vendored source, which sidesteps the ambiguity. Bundles Mosek (commercial, separate license) in third_party. If vendoring code for the runnable path, contact authors or use the OSQP fork (also unlicensed -- same caveat).
gotchas: (1) The #1 trap: control points are stored SCALED BY 1/seg_time -- forgetting the seg_time(i) MULTIPLY feeds the cert a wrong-magnitude curve (false CERTIFIED/false reject). (2) Default _traj_order=10, NOT 5 -- route through the generic certify_segments_vs_sphere, not the quintic-only certify_traj_vs_sphere. (3) Column layout per row is block [all-x | all-y | all-z] with ctrl_num1D=order+1 -- do NOT interleave xyz. (4) traj_order/min_order are rosparams -- read traj_order from the same dump, never hard-code. (5) corridor[i].t (seg_time) is the only timing source; if a dump omits it the BSeg timing is undefined. (6) Btraj minimizes snap (min_order=3) by default; irrelevant to the cert but affects which trajectories you collect.

name: EGO-Planner-v2 (MINCO degree-5, ZJU-FAST-Lab)
license: GPLv3 (same family as the EGO-v1 we already vendor)
trajectory_format: poly_traj::Trajectory (NOT templated; fixed degree 5 MINCO min-jerk), defined header-only in swarm-playground/main_ws/src/planner/traj_opt/include/optimizer/poly_traj_utils.hpp. Committed trajectory = LocalTrajData::traj (traj_utils/include/traj_utils/plan_container.hpp; also has duration, start_time world-clock). API: traj.getPieceNum(); traj.getDurations() -> Eigen::VectorXd; traj.getTotalDuration(); piece access traj[i] / traj.getPiece(i) -> poly_traj::Piece; Piece::getCoeffMat() -> const CoefficientMat& where typedef Eigen::Matrix<double,3,6> CoefficientMat (rows=x,y,z). CRITICAL ordering: eval is `tn=1; for(i=5;i>=0;i--){pos+=tn*col(i); tn*=t;}` so p(t)=Σ col(5-j)*t^j with t ABSOLUTE in [0, getDurations()[i]] -> col(0)=coeff of t^5 (HIGHEST), col(5)=constant (DESCENDING power order). MinJerkOpt::getTraj() yields this Trajectory after each optimize.
adapter_to_bseg: Native MINCO degree-5 -> our degree-5 Bernstein through the SAME fixed deg-5 C2B matrix already in bernstein_cert.hpp (C2B_int(), entries /60). It is literally minco_to_segments with ONE pre-step (column reversal + absolute-time scaling), because EGO-v2 stores DESCENDING power order while our MinjerkTraj stores ASCENDING. Per piece i: T = getDurations()[i]; C = traj[i].getCoeffMat(); for coord in {0,1,2}: ascending monomial m_j(coord)=C(coord, 5-j) for j=0..5; scaled coeff a_j = m_j * T^j; Bernstein ctrl pt b_k(coord) = Σ_{j=0}^{5} (C2B_int[k][j]/60)*a_j for k=0..5 (this is exactly the scaled-monomial->Bernstein deg-5 map: b_k=Σ_{j<=k} [C(k,j)/C(5,j)] a_j). Emit BSeg{ bern[k]={b_k(x),b_k(y),b_k(z)} (k=0..5), dur=T, t0=Σ_{i'<i} getDurations()[i'] }. Segment timing is trajectory-LOCAL (cumulative piece durations); feed KF obstacle predictions in the same local frame (subtract LocalTrajData::start_time) exactly as ego_capi already does. Then certify_segments_vs_sphere / certify_segments_above_plane run UNCHANGED (n=5 >=2).
runnable: output-only-cert (primary, ~10h); upgradeable to fully-runnable in-loop (~32h, reusing the EGO-v1 de-ROS scaffold)
build_or_bridge: OUTPUT-ONLY-CERT (recommended): vendor ONLY poly_traj_utils.hpp (header-only, pure Eigen, zero ROS). Obtain a committed poly_traj::Trajectory either (a) by dumping getCoeffMat()/getDurations() per piece from a recorded EGO-v2 run to CSV/binary and replaying through a ~30-line adapter that builds BSeg + calls our cert, or (b) by linking poly_traj_utils.hpp into a tiny standalone driver that instantiates MinJerkOpt directly. No Gurobi/Mosek/ROS needed. FULLY-RUNNABLE upgrade (if you want EGO-v2 in the MetaUrban loop for in-loop A/B like ego_capi.so): de-ROS traj_opt (poly_traj_optimizer.{h,cpp} + poly_traj_utils.hpp) + plan_env/grid_map + path_searching, replace ros::NodeHandle param loads with a config struct, expose ego2_capi.so mirroring ego/capi/ego_capi.cpp (ego2_replan/ego2_traj_eval/ego2_certify[_horizontal/_above]). Reuse the existing EGO-v1 ros_shim.h + GridMapConfig + build_segs pattern verbatim.
vendor_files: Minimal (output-only): swarm-playground/main_ws/src/planner/traj_opt/include/optimizer/poly_traj_utils.hpp + Eigen only. Fully-runnable add: traj_opt/{include/optimizer/poly_traj_optimizer.h, src/poly_traj_optimizer.cpp}, plan_env/grid_map.{h,cpp}, path_searching (kinodynamic A* / dyn_a_star), traj_utils/include/traj_utils/plan_container.hpp, the lbfgs.hpp. DROP: every plan_manage ROS node (ego_replan_fsm, the rosNode/traj_server), swarm_bridge, rviz/odom_visualization, mockamap & uav_simulator, assigner/formation modules.
advantage: Proves the certificate is solver-agnostic across trajectory REPRESENTATIONS, not just across our own code: our shipped EGO-v1 wrap is a cubic uniform B-spline, whereas EGO-v2 is a degree-5 MINCO direct spatial-temporal optimization (current SOTA from the ZJU swarm line). Certifying an INDEPENDENT lab's MINCO output through the identical deg-5 C2B path used by our own min-jerk core is the strongest single demonstration of planner-agnosticism, and EGO-v2 is the high-performance baseline reviewers will expect to see.
gotchas: (1) Column order is DESCENDING (col 0 = t^5, col 5 = constant) -- opposite of our internal MinjerkTraj; you MUST reverse before applying the ascending C2B or you get garbage. (2) getPos uses ABSOLUTE time t in [0, T_i], not normalized [0,1], so scale a_j = m_j * T_i^j with T_i=getDurations()[i]. (3) MINCO solves in world frame; set BSeg.t0 from cumulative piece durations (local), and shift obstacle prediction time by LocalTrajData::start_time. (4) poly_traj_utils.hpp is header-only and ROS-free -- vendoring just it is enough for output-only; the optimizer + grid_map are the ROS-heavy parts. (5) GPLv3: vendoring v2 code makes that boundary GPL (we already accept this for EGO-v1). (6) degree 5 >= 2 so the cert's n>=2 guard is satisfied; reuse maxdepth=16.

name: FASTER (MIT-ACL, Gurobi min-jerk)
license: BSD 3-Clause (permissive; vendor-friendly) -- same lab as the SANDO baseline we already carry
trajectory_format: SolverGurobi (faster/include/solverGurobi.hpp + faster/src/solverGurobi.cpp). Minimum-jerk TRIPLE-INTEGRATOR (control = jerk, jerk CONSTANT per interval) over N_ equal-duration intervals of length dt_ (dt_ recomputed each solve by findDT; all intervals share it; N_ via setN). Per interval t, axis ii in {0,1,2} position is CUBIC. Numeric coeffs read AFTER optimize() via Gurobi .getValue(): getAn(t,ii)=x[t][0+ii]*dt_^3, getBn=x[t][3+ii]*dt_^2, getCn=x[t][6+ii]*dt_, getDn=x[t][9+ii] give the SCALED coeffs of p(s)=An*s^3+Bn*s^2+Cn*s+Dn on s in [0,1]. Raw absolute form: p(tau)=x[t][0+ii]*tau^3+x[t][3+ii]*tau^2+x[t][6+ii]*tau+x[t][9+ii], tau in [0,dt_]. fillX() samples this into a std::vector<state> (pos/vel/accel/jerk). The COMMITTED trajectory FASTER flies = sg_whole_ (whole traj) stitched with sg_safe_ (known-free stopping traj); read coeffs/dt_/N_ from EACH solver.
adapter_to_bseg: Cubic monomial -> degree-3 Bernstein (same n=3 family our EGO-v1 B-spline->Bezier output already produces, so the cert path is byte-for-byte reused). Per interval t, per axis ii: scaled ascending monomial coeffs (a0,a1,a2,a3) = (getDn, getCn, getBn, getAn)(t,ii) [equivalently from raw vars: a_j = x[t][3*(3-j)+ii] * dt_^j]. Apply the fixed cubic scaled-monomial->Bezier matrix M3 = [[1,0,0,0],[1,1/3,0,0],[1,2/3,1/3,0],[1,1,1,1]] (b_k=Σ_{j<=k}[C(k,j)/C(3,j)]a_j): b0=Dn; b1=Dn+Cn/3; b2=Dn+2*Cn/3+Bn/3; b3=Dn+Cn+Bn+An. Emit BSeg{ bern[k]={b_k(x),b_k(y),b_k(z)} (k=0..3), dur=dt_, t0=t*dt_ (offset by sg_whole_ total duration when appending sg_safe_ intervals) }. License-free alternative (no Gurobi): from the published `state` stream use jerk-const-per-interval -> per interval start (p0,v0,a0) and constant jerk j: ascending monomial m0=p0,m1=v0,m2=a0/2,m3=j/6; scaled a_j=m_j*dt_^j; same M3. certify_segments_vs_sphere / certify_segments_above_plane run UNCHANGED (n=3 >=2).
runnable: output-only-cert (full standalone build is Gurobi-license + ROS heavy; not needed to certify FASTER's emitted trajectory)
build_or_bridge: OUTPUT-ONLY-CERT: do NOT build FASTER for the cert (it needs a Gurobi license + ROS1 + JPS3D + DecompUtil). Two feeds: (a) instrument FASTER's replan() right after sg_whole_.fillX()/sg_safe_ to dump per-interval coeffs (getAn..getDn or raw x[t][0..11]) + dt_ + N_ per solver to CSV/JSON; (b) license-free: subscribe to / replay the published goal `state` trajectory (pos/vel/accel/jerk) and reconstruct cubics via the jerk-const formula. Then a ~40-line adapter (Python over an ego_bridge-style ctypes capi, or direct C++) builds the BSeg list and calls sando::bcert::certify_segments_vs_sphere/_above_plane. A FULLY-RUNNABLE port (Gurobi + de-ROS so FASTER runs inside MetaUrban) is ~40h+ and only worth it if you need to RUN FASTER, not just certify it.
vendor_files: Output-only needs NO FASTER source -- only an adapter ingesting the dumped coeffs or the published state stream. If you instrument the dump: faster/include/{solverGurobi.hpp, faster_types.hpp} + faster/src/solverGurobi.cpp (+ Gurobi headers) to read getAn..getDn after optimize(). DROP everything else for certification: faster_ros.cpp, jps_manager, read_map, thirdparty/DecompROS, thirdparty/jps3d, rviz, and all ROS nodes (main.cpp).
advantage: Different safety PHILOSOPHY and different solver CLASS than anything we wrap: MIT-ACL's convex (Gurobi QP) minimum-jerk planner whose own safety argument is to always keep a known-free stopping trajectory (Free-Known vs Unknown space decomposition). Certifying FASTER lets us show our CONTINUOUS-time Bernstein certificate catches whether its inherently DISCRETE-time safety actually holds between samples, on a degree-3 polynomial from a QP solver (not a B-spline or MINCO). It is BSD-3 (clean to vendor) and from the same lab as the SANDO baseline we already carry -- a natural, reviewer-expected baseline that broadens the agnosticism claim to convex-optimization planners.
gotchas: (1) Committed traj is STITCHED: sg_whole_ then sg_safe_ -- certify the concatenation, not just sg_whole_; each is N_ equal-dt_ cubic intervals, so append with a running t0 (and note dt_ can DIFFER between the two solvers; read dt_ from each). (2) Coeffs are Gurobi GRBLinExpr -- only valid AFTER optimize(); read via .getValue() / GRB_DoubleAttr_X. (3) getAn/Bn/Cn/Dn are ALREADY scaled to s in [0,1] (An=a*dt_^3 etc.), so feed them straight into M3 with NO extra dt scaling; only the raw x[t][] form needs the *dt_^j scaling. (4) To avoid the Gurobi license entirely, reconstruct from the published state stream (jerk const per interval) -- exact, not a fit. (5) cubic degree 3 >= 2 so the cert's n>=2 guard holds; identical to our EGO-v1 Bezier output so certify_segments_* needs no change.

name: mav_trajectory_generation (ethz-asl, Richter/Bry/Roy min-snap polynomial QP)
license: Apache-2.0 (core pkg mav_trajectory_generation). Clean to vendor.
trajectory_format: Build: mav_trajectory_generation::PolynomialOptimization<N> opt(3); opt.setupFromVertices(vertices, segment_times, derivative_order::SNAP); opt.solveLinear(); then opt.getSegments(&segs) -> mav_trajectory_generation::Segment::Vector (== std::vector<Segment>) OR opt.getTrajectory(&traj) then traj.getSegments(&segs). Per Segment: seg.getTime() -> double (segment DURATION in seconds), seg.N() -> int (#coeffs = order; default N=10 => degree 9), seg.D() -> int (=3), seg[d] -> const Polynomial& (d=0,1,2). Per Polynomial: seg[d].getCoefficients(0) -> Eigen::VectorXd of length N, MONOMIAL basis, constant term first: p_d(tau)=a0 + a1*tau + ... + a_{N-1}*tau^{N-1}. CRITICAL (verified in src/trajectory.cpp evaluate): tau is segment-local time in ABSOLUTE SECONDS, tau in [0, seg.getTime()], NOT normalized to [0,1]; evaluate() calls segments_[i].evaluate(t - accumulated_time). solveLinear() internally rescales for conditioning but getSegments() returns real-second polynomials (do not re-apply scaling).
adapter_to_bseg: Basis change = MONOMIAL -> BERNSTEIN of degree n=N-1 (default n=9). For each segment i (cumulative start time t0_cum = running sum of getTime()): set BSeg.t0 = t0_cum, BSeg.dur = T = seg.getTime(), BSeg.bern has n+1 = N control points. For each dim d in {0,1,2}: (1) read a = seg[d].getCoefficients(0) (length N, c0 first); (2) reparam tau = s*T, s in [0,1], giving scaled monomial coeffs atil_j = a[j] * pow(T,j); (3) power->Bernstein: B_k(d) = sum_{j=0..k} ( C(k,j)/C(n,j) ) * atil_j, for k=0..n. C(k,j)=0 for j>k so only j<=k contributes. Use sando::bcert::g_binom for the binomials. This is EXACTLY sando::bcert::C2B_int generalized to degree 9 (verified: for n=5 the formula reproduces C2B_int[k][j]/60 byte-for-byte, e.g. B_2 = atil0 + (2/5)atil1 + (1/10)atil2 = rows {1,0.4,0.1,...}). Push each BSeg into std::vector<BSeg> in segment order; M segments -> M BSegs. Then call sando::bcert::certify_segments_vs_sphere / _above_plane unchanged (it already handles arbitrary degree via g_square/g_elevate: deg-9 position -> deg-18 squared deficit). For exact soundness, do the scale+matrix in the iv_* interval arithmetic (atil_j as iv_mul over an iv power chain of T) so high T^9 magnitudes stay outward-rounded.
vendor_files: Vendor only the CORE pkg subtree mav_trajectory_generation/ (drop the entire mav_trajectory_generation_ros/ pkg = rviz, yaml IO, ros msgs, nodes). Headers: include/mav_trajectory_generation/{polynomial.h, segment.h, trajectory.h, vertex.h, motion_defines.h, polynomial_optimization_linear.h, convolution.h, extremum.h}. Sources: src/{polynomial.cpp, segment.cpp, trajectory.cpp, vertex.cpp, motion_defines.cpp, polynomial_optimization_linear.cpp}. DROP: polynomial_optimization_nonlinear.{h,cpp} (the ONLY nlopt user -> verified linear path needs no nlopt), timing.h, io.{h,cpp} (yaml), trajectory_sampling, rpoly_ak1.{h,cpp}/rpoly/ (root finder used ONLY by Polynomial::getRoots/getExtrema, which the BSeg adapter never calls). Deps reduce to Eigen + glog only.
build_or_bridge: Standalone g++/CMake, mirroring ego_capi.so. glog is the only non-Eigen dep and is used purely as CHECK/LOG macros -> either apt-get install libgoogle-glog-dev, or drop in a ~12-line shim glog/logging.h defining CHECK(x), CHECK_*(a,b), LOG(x) as no-ops/asserts (removes the dependency entirely). Write mtg_capi.cpp exposing extern "C": mtg_create(), mtg_set_vertices(double* waypoints, int n_wp), mtg_solve(double v_max,double a_max) [calls estimateSegmentTimes + solveLinear], mtg_n_segments(), mtg_get_segment(int i, double* t0_dur_out, double* bern_out) [runs the monomial->Bernstein adapter above and returns the per-segment Bernstein cps + (t0,dur)], and mtg_certify(...)/mtg_certify_above(...) that build std::vector<BSeg> internally and call sando::bcert exactly like ego_certify. Build line (mirror EGO): g++ -O2 -shared -fPIC -std=c++17 -w -o capi/mtg_capi.so capi/mtg_capi.cpp src/*.cpp -I include -I ../cpp/include -I ../cpp/third_party/eigen -lglog. Drive from Python via ctypes (clone ego_bridge.py). runnable as a real planner because solveLinear is a closed-form linear solve (no Gurobi/Mosek/nlopt/ROS).
runnable: fully-runnable (vendor the LINEAR core only: solveLinear is a closed-form unconstrained QP, no nlopt/ROS/Gurobi). Can degrade to output-only-cert: dump one Trajectory's segments to a coeff file and certify offline if you don't want to build at all.
advantage: THE canonical classical min-snap polynomial baseline (Richter/Bry/Roy, the single most-cited rotary-wing trajectory method) and a fundamentally DIFFERENT paradigm from EGO/MINCO: a global unconstrained-QP polynomial through fixed waypoints with NO corridor/obstacle term. It is the key high-degree stress test of our planner-agnostic claim: default degree-9 segments push the cert to a deg-18 squared-deficit (vs cubic/quintic today), proving the Bernstein core is genuinely degree-agnostic and numerically sound at high order. Reviewers expect this baseline; certifying it (and rejecting the bare waypoint trajectory through a pedestrian, then letting our maneuver tournament reroute) is a strong external-validity result.
gotchas: (1) glog CHECK macros are sprinkled throughout -> link glog or shim it. (2) High degree: atil_j = a_j*T^j with T^9 grows fast; do the scale+matrix in iv_* interval arithmetic so margins stay SOUND (cert is already adaptive de Casteljau, but tighten by feeding intervals). (3) solveLinear internally normalizes segment times for conditioning but getSegments() returns real-second polys — do NOT double-scale. (4) It plans through FIXED waypoints with no obstacle awareness, so as a go-around baseline you either supply detour waypoints or (cleaner) treat it output-only and let our tournament pick the maneuver. (5) Endpoint derivatives may be left free; returned segments are still concrete polynomials, adapter unaffected. (6) Keep N a compile-time template (PolynomialOptimization<10>); pick N=10 for snap, N=8 for jerk.

name: RapidQuadrocopterTrajectories (Mueller, closed-form quintic motion primitive)
license: GPL-3.0 (COPYING.txt). Viral: keep it as an ISOLATED optional capi loaded only at eval time; do NOT statically link into our shipped Apache/our-core cert lib.
trajectory_format: C++ folder verified to contain RapidTrajectoryGenerator.{h,cpp}, SingleAxisTrajectory.{h,cpp}, Vec3.h, RootFinder/. API: RapidTrajectoryGenerator traj(Vec3 x0, Vec3 v0, Vec3 a0, Vec3 gravity); traj.SetGoalPosition(Vec3)/SetGoalVelocity(Vec3)/SetGoalAcceleration(Vec3) (or per-axis SetGoal*InAxis, or leave free); traj.Generate(double timeToGo). Output coeffs: per axis i in {0,1,2}: traj.GetAxisParamAlpha(i)/Beta(i)/Gamma(i) -> double, plus per-axis SingleAxisTrajectory _axis[i] with GetParamAlpha/Beta/Gamma() and GetInitialPosition/Velocity/Acceleration(). Each axis is a SINGLE degree-5 polynomial in ABSOLUTE local seconds t in [0, timeToGo]: p_d(t) = p0 + v0*t + (a0/2)*t^2 + (gamma/6)*t^3 + (beta/24)*t^4 + (alpha/120)*t^5. M=1 segment per Generate(). Also Vec3 GetPosition(double t) for sampling.
adapter_to_bseg: Basis change = MONOMIAL -> BERNSTEIN of degree 5 -> REUSE sando::bcert::C2B_int() directly (Mueller's quintic is the SAME degree as MINCO; no new matrix needed). Build ONE BSeg (BSeg.t0 = 0 if it is the committed primitive, or cumulative start if chaining primitives; BSeg.dur = T = timeToGo; BSeg.bern size 6). For each dim d: (1) monomial coeffs in increasing power order c = { p0_d, v0_d, 0.5*a0_d, GetAxisParamGamma(d)/6.0, GetAxisParamBeta(d)/24.0, GetAxisParamAlpha(d)/120.0 } (p0/v0/a0 from the x0/v0/a0 you passed in, or GetInitial*()); (2) scale to s in [0,1]: atil_j = c[j]*pow(T,j); (3) Bernstein cps: B_k(d) = sum_{j=0..5} (C2B_int()[k][j]/60.0) * atil_j, k=0..5. This is byte-identical to the MINCO path in certify_traj_vs_sphere (a[j]=c*Ti^j then C2B[k][j]/60). Push the BSeg(s) and call certify_segments_vs_sphere/_above_plane unchanged. For chained multi-primitive go-arounds, emit one BSeg per primitive with cumulative t0.
vendor_files: Vendor 5 files, zero ROS, zero Eigen, zero map: C++/{RapidTrajectoryGenerator.h, RapidTrajectoryGenerator.cpp, SingleAxisTrajectory.h, SingleAxisTrajectory.cpp, Vec3.h}. DROP Demo.cpp. RootFinder/ (Rapid Collision Detection, arXiv:1904.04223) is OPTIONAL — vendor it only if you also want to A/B Mueller's own feasibility/collision check against our continuous-time cert; the BSeg adapter does not need it. Only dependency is <math.h>.
build_or_bridge: Trivial standalone. Write rqt_capi.cpp exposing extern "C": rqt_generate(double* x0,double* v0,double* a0,double* gp,double* gv,double* ga,double Tf, double* t0_dur_out, double* bern_out) that constructs RapidTrajectoryGenerator, sets goals, Generate(Tf), runs the deg-5 C2B adapter and returns 6 Bernstein cps + (0,Tf); plus rqt_certify(...) building the BSeg and calling sando::bcert exactly like ego_certify. Build (mirror EGO, no Eigen needed for the planner itself; include our cert headers which use Eigen): g++ -O2 -shared -fPIC -std=c++17 -w -o capi/rqt_capi.so capi/rqt_capi.cpp RapidTrajectoryGenerator.cpp SingleAxisTrajectory.cpp -I . -I ../cpp/include -I ../cpp/third_party/eigen. Drive via ctypes (clone ego_bridge.py). Convert Eigen<->Vec3 only at the capi boundary.
runnable: fully-runnable (tiny pure-C++ closed-form generator, no optimizer/map/ROS — generation is microseconds).
advantage: Mueller's computationally-efficient closed-form motion primitive — the canonical state-to-state / interception primitive used in sampling-based MPC and reactive avoidance (generate thousands of candidate primitives to a sampled goal set, keep the feasible/cheapest). Two distinct wins: (1) its degree-5 EXACTLY matches MINCO, so it validates the C2B_int reuse and is the cheapest possible second planner to graft (~3h). (2) Its native 'spray many primitives at sampled goals' workflow maps PERFECTLY onto our maneuver/go-around tournament: each candidate primitive becomes a BSeg, we certify each against the KF-predicted moving sphere/cylinder, and pick the fastest CERTIFIED one — i.e. Mueller emits candidates and OUR continuous-time cert is the selector, a clean demonstration of the certified fastest-safe go-around with a third-party primitive generator. Bonus baseline: A/B our cert vs Mueller's own Rapid Collision Detection feasibility check.
gotchas: (1) GPL-3.0 — isolate in its own rqt_capi.so loaded at eval time; never link into the shipped cert/core lib. (2) Single segment per Generate(); chain primitives for multi-leg go-arounds (cumulative t0). (3) Uses its own Vec3, not Eigen — convert at the boundary. (4) The gravity Vec3 in the ctor only affects feasibility checks (thrust/body-rate limits), NOT the position polynomial — pass (0,0,-9.81) or (0,0,0), position coeffs are unaffected. (5) Goal derivatives can be left free (omit SetGoal*); alpha/beta/gamma are still returned and the coeffs are valid. (6) t is absolute seconds in [0,Tf]; remember the T^j scale step when going to s in [0,1].

name: Motion Primitive Library (sikang/motion_primitive_library; core of mpl_ros)
license: Apache-2.0 (confirmed via GitHub license API). Permissive — safe to vendor into sando-core, unlike Fast-Planner's GPL.
trajectory_format: Search-based kinodynamic planner. Build MPL::VoxelMapPlanner (= MapPlanner<3>, from include/mpl_planner/planner/map_planner.h), call planner->plan(Waypoint<3> start, Waypoint<3> goal) -> bool, then planner->getTraj() -> Trajectory<3> (defined include/mpl_basis/trajectory.h). Trajectory<3>::getPrimitives() returns vec_E<Primitive<3>> (also the public member `segs`); per-segment duration via Primitive<3>::t() -> decimal_t (or Trajectory::getSegmentTimes()), total via getTotalTime(). Each Primitive<3> exposes axis k via pr(int k) -> Primitive1D; Primitive1D::coeff() -> Vec6f c with the EXACT power-basis form p(tau)=c(0)/120*tau^5 + c(1)/24*tau^4 + c(2)/6*tau^3 + c(3)/2*tau^2 + c(4)*tau + c(5), tau in [0, t()]. So the committed trajectory is piecewise degree<=5 MONOMIAL polynomial per axis (degree 3 for the default jerk-input primitives; higher coeffs are exactly 0).
adapter_to_bseg: Basis change = monomial(local-time)->Bernstein(deg 5), BYTE-IDENTICAL to our existing minco_to_segments C2B path (same fixed C2B_int matrix). Concretely write mpl_to_segments(const Trajectory<3>& tr): cum=0; for each seg in tr.getPrimitives(): T=seg.t(); for axis k in {0,1,2}: Vec6f c=seg.pr(k).coeff(); convert coeff()'s scaled form to plain monomial coeffs a_j (coeff of tau^j): a0=c(5), a1=c(4), a2=c(3)/2, a3=c(2)/6, a4=c(1)/24, a5=c(0)/120. Rescale to s in [0,1] (tau=s*T): A_j = a_j * T^j (j=0..5). Then Bernstein P_k = sum_{j<=k} (C2B_int()[k][j]/60.0)*A_j for k=0..5 (this is exactly P_k = sum_j C(k,j)/C(5,j) * A_j; verified C2B_int[k][j]==60*C(k,j)/C(5,j)). Set BSeg.bern[k]=(P_k.x,P_k.y,P_k.z) (Vector3d), BSeg.t0=cum, BSeg.dur=T; cum+=T. Emit 6 control points always (deg-5 container; a degree-3 jerk primitive lands as its degree-elevated cubic — our cert needs degree>=2, satisfied). Timing maps directly: segments are sequential in the trajectory's own time frame starting at 0, dur=Primitive::t(), so c(t)=c0+vel*t+0.5*acc*t^2 obstacle poly is in the same frame with zero offset. Then certify_segments_vs_sphere / _horizontal / _above_plane run unchanged. Free sanity check: a static-obstacle MPL traj must give the SAME verdict whether fed via this path or by stuffing the same monomial coeffs into a MinjerkTraj and calling minco_to_segments.
build_or_bridge: Build the standalone core lib: `git clone`, `apt install libeigen3-dev libboost-dev` (Boost only for boost::heap d_ary open-list; OpenCV+yaml-cpp are TEST-ONLY, skip them), `mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make -j4` (README-confirmed standalone, no ROS). Then write mpl_capi.cpp mirroring ego_capi.cpp: (1) mpl_create() -> new MPL::VoxelMapPlanner(false); set planner->setVmax/setAmax/setDt/setTmax and planner->setU(U) where U=vec_E<VecDf> of discretized jerk inputs (the test builds U as the {-u,0,+u}^3 grid). (2) mpl_set_gridmap + mpl_update_cloud build a std::shared_ptr<MPL::VoxelMapUtil> and call map_util->setMap(Vecf<3> origin, Veci<3> dim, std::vector<signed char> data, decimal_t res) marking each predicted-occupancy point's voxel = 100 (val_occ); planner->setMapUtil(map_util). This is the direct analog of ego_set_gridmap/ego_update_cloud — same predicted point cloud we already feed EGO. (3) mpl_replan(sp,sv,sa,gp,gv): fill Waypoint<3> start/goal (set pos/vel/acc + use_pos/use_vel/use_acc/use_jrk flags), bool ok=planner->plan(start,goal). (4) mpl_certify*(...): segs=mpl_to_segments(planner->getTraj()), call the SAME sando::bcert::certify_segments_vs_sphere/_horizontal/_above_plane, return verdict+margin. Compile exactly like ego_capi: `g++ -O2 -shared -fPIC -std=c++17 -o mpl_capi.so mpl_capi.cpp <mpl src/*.cpp> -Iinclude -I../cpp/include -I../cpp/third_party/eigen -I../cpp/third_party`. Bridge: copy metaurban/ego_bridge.py -> mpl_bridge.py, swap the ctypes symbol names (mpl_create/mpl_set_gridmap/mpl_update_cloud/mpl_replan/mpl_certify...). Drives straight into the existing maneuver tournament harness.
vendor_files: Copy motion_primitive_library/include/** (mpl_basis/*.h: trajectory.h, primitive.h, waypoint.h, math.h; mpl_planner/**: map_planner.h, graph_search.h, env_map.h, state_space.h; mpl_collision/map_util.h) + the matching src/*.cpp under src/mpl_planner (graph_search.cpp, map_planner.cpp). DROP: the entire mpl_ros/ ROS wrapper, test/ (opencv_drawing.hpp, read_map.hpp, timer.hpp, all OpenCV+yaml-cpp deps), docs/. Add one new file ego/../mpl/capi/mpl_capi.cpp. No map front-end needed — voxel map is built from our predicted point cloud.
advantage: DIFFERENT PLANNER FAMILY: it is a deterministic, resolution-complete GRAPH SEARCH over closed-form motion primitives (forward-integrated jerk polynomials), not a gradient/QP B-spline optimizer like EGO and Fast-Planner. Adding it proves the cert is planner-AGNOSTIC across an entire second paradigm (search vs optimization), not just across two B-spline cousins. Its output is already an exact piecewise MONOMIAL polynomial, so it directly exercises (and re-validates) the same C2B monomial->Bernstein path our own MINCO uses — strongest possible evidence the BSeg seam is the planner's native representation, not a refit. It is the canonical search-based SE(3)/kinodynamic UAV baseline (Liu RA-L'18), so reviewers expect it; and because primitives are constructed dynamically-feasible by design, it is a clean fastest-vs-safe speed competitor for the go-around A/B.
gotchas: (1) coeff() returns the SCALED form (c0/120, c1/24, ...), NOT plain monomial coeffs — must divide by 120/24/6/2/1/1 before the C2B step (a common off-by-factorial bug). (2) The Vec6f orders highest power first: c(0) multiplies tau^5, c(5) is the constant — reverse vs our MinjerkTraj's low-first convention, so a_j=...; double-check by evaluating p(0)==BSeg.bern[0] and p(T)==BSeg.bern[5]. (3) Primitive duration t() is per-segment LOCAL time; segments are contiguous so just accumulate — no virtual/actual tau-vs-Ts remapping needed for position (taus/Ts are only for the time-optimal traj_solver path). (4) VoxelMapUtil dilation/inflation: setMap stores raw occupancy; call the planner's own inflation OR pre-inflate the cloud so the search avoids the same tube the cert checks. (5) Boost d_ary_heap header must be on the include path.

name: Fast-Planner (HKUST-Aerial-Robotics/Fast-Planner; kinodynamic + B-spline-opt, the academic parent of EGO)
license: GPL-3.0 (confirmed via GitHub license API). IMPORTANT: copyleft — do NOT statically vendor its source into a shippable sando-core build. Mitigation baked into the recommended path below: consume only the EMITTED control-points + knot vector (plain numbers, not copyrightable) and run OUR OWN knot-insertion, so zero GPL code is linked into our cert.
trajectory_format: Committed trajectory = a NonUniformBspline (fast_planner/bspline/include/bspline/non_uniform_bspline.h). FastPlannerManager::kinodynamicReplan(start_pt,start_vel,start_acc,end_pt,end_vel) (or topoReplan) writes the result into public member local_data_ (struct LocalTrajData, plan_container.hpp), whose member NonUniformBspline position_traj_ IS the committed position curve (also velocity_traj_/acceleration_traj_/yaw_traj_, plus traj_id_, duration_, start_time_). NonUniformBspline is a UNIFORM-DEGREE (p_=3, cubic) but generally NON-UNIFORM-KNOT B-spline: members control_points_ (Eigen::MatrixXd, N x 3, each ROW is one 3-D control point), int p_ (=3), int m_ (=n_+p_+1), Eigen::VectorXd u_ (knot vector), double interval_. Accessors: getControlPoint() -> MatrixXd, getKnot() -> VectorXd, getInterval() -> double, getTimeSpan(double& um,double& um_p) (um=u_(p_), um_p=u_(m_-p_) = valid knot domain), evaluateDeBoorT(t) (= evaluateDeBoor(t+u_(p_))). Knots become genuinely non-uniform after reallocateTime()/lengthenTime() (the dynamic-feasibility time stretch), confirmed in non_uniform_bspline.cpp — so this is NOT EGO's uniform case.
adapter_to_bseg: Basis change = per-knot-span Bezier (Bernstein) EXTRACTION via Boehm knot insertion (the GENERAL case; EGO's fixed Mb/6 matrix is only the uniform-knot specialization). Write fastplanner_to_segments(const MatrixXd& P, const VectorXd& u, int p=3): trajectory time origin is t=0 <-> knot u(p) (because evaluateDeBoorT adds u(p_)). For each valid span i = p .. m-p-1 (m=u.size()-1; gives m-2p segments): the cubic curve on [u_i,u_{i+1}] is governed by the p+1=4 local control points rows P_{i-p}..P_i; obtain its 4 Bezier control points Q_0..Q_3 (on normalized s in [0,1] over the span) by inserting BOTH endpoint knots u_i and u_{i+1} of this span up to multiplicity p via Boehm's recurrence (Q computed from D=[P_{i-3..i}] with alphas alpha = (xi - u_a)/(u_b - u_a) using only the local knots u_{i-2..i+3}; closed-form 4x4 extraction operator depends on the two adjacent knot intervals). Set BSeg.bern={Q_0,Q_1,Q_2,Q_3} (already Vector3d rows), BSeg.t0 = u(i) - u(p), BSeg.dur = u(i+1) - u(i). Feed the vector<BSeg> straight into certify_segments_vs_sphere/_horizontal/_above_plane unchanged. Timing maps exactly: obstacle poly c(t)=c0+vel*t+0.5*acc*t^2 is in the same t-from-0 frame. FREE unit test guaranteeing correctness: on a UNIFORM knot vector our extraction operator MUST reproduce EGO's Mb={{1,4,1,0},{0,4,2,0},{0,2,4,0},{0,1,4,1}}/6 exactly (already coded in ego_capi.cpp build_segs) — assert equality to pin the non-uniform generalization.
build_or_bridge: PRIMARY (output-only-cert, ~license-clean, ~5h): we do NOT build the heavy Fast-Planner stack. Two sub-options to obtain a real committed NonUniformBspline: (a) run stock Fast-Planner once in its ROS sim and record the published B-spline (control_points + knot vector u_, e.g. from the bspline/Bspline topic or a one-line std::ofstream dump of getControlPoint()/getKnot() in the traj_server), save to .npy/.csv — then our standalone reads CPs+knots and runs OUR fastplanner_to_segments + cert (no Fast-Planner code linked at all). (b) Self-contained, zero-ROS: vendor ONLY non_uniform_bspline.{h,cpp} (Eigen-only, ~2 files), construct a uniform NonUniformBspline from a waypoint path, call reallocateTime() (vendored, Eigen-only) to manufacture the genuine NON-uniform committed curve, then extract+certify — this exercises the non-uniform path with no GPL beyond the 2 vendored files (keep them out of the shipped lib; treat as a test fixture). STRETCH (fully-runnable, ~+25h): de-ROS kinodynamicReplan like we did EGO — Fast-Planner is EGO's direct ancestor and shares bspline/ + plan_env/sdf_map + path_searching/kinodynamic_astar + bspline_opt(NLopt). Reuse the ego/ ros::NodeHandle shims; build fp_capi.so exposing fp_create/fp_set_gridmap/fp_update_cloud/fp_replan/fp_certify mirroring ego_capi.cpp. Heavier because it adds NLopt + the EDT/SDF map + kinodynamic A* search; only worth it if a closed-loop go-around A/B vs Fast-Planner (not just certifying its output) is required.
vendor_files: PRIMARY: vendor at most fast_planner/bspline/include/bspline/non_uniform_bspline.h + fast_planner/bspline/src/non_uniform_bspline.cpp (Eigen-only) as a TEST fixture; better, vendor NOTHING and consume emitted CPs+knots. Add our own fastplanner_bezier_extract.hpp (Boehm) in cpp/include/sando_cpp/. DROP for the primary path: plan_env (sdf_map, edt_environment, raycast), path_searching (kinodynamic_astar, topo_prm), bspline_opt (BsplineOptimizer + NLopt), plan_manage (planner_manager, FSM nodes, traj_server), all rviz/ROS msgs. STRETCH build additionally keeps bspline_opt (link libnlopt-dev), path_searching/kinodynamic_astar, plan_env/sdf_map+edt — de-ROS'd; still DROP the FSM/traj_server ROS nodes and depth/odom topic plumbing (replace with fp_update_cloud like ego).
advantage: It is the canonical NON-UNIFORM cubic B-spline UAV planner and the direct academic ancestor of EGO (Zhou et al. RA-L'19, 1k+ citations) — the reviewer-expected B-spline baseline. Critically it is the planner that FORCES and validates our GENERAL Bezier-extraction adapter: after reallocateTime() the committed knots are non-uniform, so EGO's fixed Mb/6 matrix is INVALID and the cert must use true knot-insertion. Certifying Fast-Planner therefore demonstrates the BSeg seam handles the realistic post-time-reallocation non-uniform case, not just textbook uniform B-splines — a strictly stronger planner-agnostic claim than EGO alone. And because it is GPL/ROS-heavy, the output-only-cert route also showcases the 'certify a foreign committed trajectory without building the planner' capability that is the whole point of the BSeg abstraction.
gotchas: (1) control_points_ is N x 3 with ROWS as points (opposite to EGO's get_control_points() which is 3 x Ncols COLUMNS) — transpose accordingly (P.row(j)). (2) Time origin is u_(p_) not 0: BSeg.t0 must subtract u(p) or the obstacle prediction will be phase-shifted by ~p*interval. (3) Non-uniform: do NOT reuse ego_capi's Mb/6 — that silently gives wrong control points on stretched spans; use the knot-dependent extraction and assert it collapses to Mb/6 on uniform knots. (4) GPL-3.0: keep any vendored non_uniform_bspline.cpp out of the shipped/linked cert build (test fixture only); the clean path consumes only numeric CPs+knots. (5) The yaw_traj_ and velocity/acceleration members are derivative B-splines — certify ONLY position_traj_; don't accidentally feed acceleration_traj_ control points. (6) reallocateTime can leave a near-zero-length span at the ends — guard BSeg.dur>0 (the cert already skips dur<=0, but extraction alphas can divide-by-zero on a repeated knot).
